passage:
"I'm going to post a reply to everyone," Gargi said, thumbs already typing. "I'll tell them exactly what I think."
"Wait," Harsha said, putting his hand over her phone. "If you post, they'll screenshot that too. It'll become bigger."
"So I just sit here?"
"No. Let me handle Vinit." Harsha opened his own chat. He typed: That isn't true. Please delete it.
"That's it?"
"That's it. No insults."
Harsha's mother came in with two plates of poha. She looked at Gargi's red eyes. "What happened, kanna?"
Gargi hesitated. Harsha nodded at her. "Tell her. And tomorrow we'll go to Rao sir together."
Gargi put her phone down and started talking.

qa.q: What message did Harsha send to Vinit?
qa.a: He typed: That isn't true. Please delete it.

qa.q: Why did Gargi want to post a reply to everyone?
qa.a: She was hurt and angry and wanted to defend herself by telling everyone exactly what she thought.

qa.q: Why does Harsha's way work better than a big public reply?
qa.a: A calm private request to the spreader does not give the rumour new fuel, and helping Gargi talk to his mother and Rao sir gets her real support.

qa.q: How might Harsha's mother feel when Gargi starts talking?
qa.a: She probably feels concerned but glad Gargi trusts her, and ready to help.

grounding: It shows a calm friend asking the spreader to delete a false story and steering the target toward a parent and teacher instead of a public denial.

passage:
I'm Akash. Last term, when that edited picture of Jahnavi went round, she wanted to make a video and "destroy them all." I understood. I was angry too. But I'd seen what happened to another girl who replied in public: fifty new comments by morning.
So I did two things. I messaged the three boys who first shared it, one by one: "It's not true. Please delete it." Two did. One laughed, but at least he stopped posting.
Then I sat with Jahnavi outside the staff room until she was ready to knock on Mrs Kulkarni's door. I didn't do the talking. I just stayed.
Looking back, the quiet stuff did more than any video could have.

qa.q: How many of the three boys deleted the picture?
qa.a: Two of the three boys deleted it.

qa.q: How did Akash feel when Jahnavi wanted to make a video?
qa.a: Akash understood and felt angry too, but was worried a public reply would bring more comments, like it had for another girl.

qa.q: Which of Akash's steps do you think helped Jahnavi most, and why?
qa.a: Sitting with her until she was ready to talk to Mrs Kulkarni, because it got her adult support without making the rumour bigger. 🙂

qa.q: What was it like for Jahnavi to have Akash wait with her outside the staff room?
qa.a: She likely felt less alone and braver, knowing a friend was beside her while she spoke for herself.

grounding: It illustrates a friend calmly asking spreaders to delete a false picture and supporting the target to reach a teacher, instead of a public denial.
